key_insight: Vectorized, high-fidelity simulation reveals that DRL can solve robotic reach and reach-avoid tasks well in benchmark settings, but performance drops in realistic scenarios.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark provides a more practical testbed for robot-arm safety and manipulation research, helping engineers evaluate whether policies generalize beyond simplified tabletop environments.
method: Built a comprehensive reach-avoid benchmark for robotic arms with realistic scenarios
Used MuJoCo MJX physics and Brax to parallelize simulation and DRL training
Evaluated multiple robot platforms and task variants, including UR5e and Franka
evidence_signal: The abstract reports state-of-the-art success rates of 96.1% and 98.8% for reach, and 86.8% and 95.2% for static reach-avoid on UR5e and Franka, respectively.
watch_item: Results are strongest for the static reach-avoid setting; the paper notes that prior simplified successes do not necessarily transfer to realistic environments, so generalization remains a concern.
paper_title: Learning Reach-Avoid Task with Reinforcement Learning: Vectorized Simulation and Benchmark
